A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main text, equations, four figures, and Appendix A.1–A.8. All 17 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: Section 3.4 and Figure 3 report original numerical Jacobian-rank estimates of normalized attention's neuromanifold dimension, compared with the conjectured formula.

after.justification: Section 3.4 and Figure 3 retain the original numerical dimension estimates and their agreement with the conjectured formula.

M1.justification: The lightning and normalized attention models, virtual-weight parametrization, and computational procedures are unchanged. The revised theorem assumption does not modify the models.

E1.justification: Both versions numerically investigate normalized deep attention using synthetic Gaussian inputs. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Both retain the same comparison between estimated dimensions and Equation 16's theoretical predictions. Neither reports competing-method benchmarks.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 retains 250 normally distributed inputs, two layers, sequence length t=3, attention dimensions a_i=2, embedding dimensions δ=3–10, and dimension estimation through Jacobian rank.

E4.justification: The embedding-dimension sweep supporting Conjecture 3.10 is unchanged. Neither version adds ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or supplementary empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Random-input and random-parameter sampling descriptions are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for Figure 3.

E6.justification: Figure 3 retains identical plotted results, and both versions report agreement between estimated and expected dimensions throughout δ=3–10. No empirical result entries or findings change.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.7 adds the hypothesis L≠0. Appendix A.6 replaces the quadratic-factor coprimality assertion with an argument invoking irreducibility and distinct powers-of-three exponents. These are localized revisions to assumptions and proof reasoning; the generic dimension formulas and other theoretical results remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same claims about generic identifiability, neuromanifold dimension, single-layer geometry, and the numerically supported conjecture for normalized deep attention.

C2.justification: The added L≠0 qualification explicitly excludes the zero composite value-map case from Theorem 3.7's applicability. Interpretations concerning sample complexity and low-rank bias, and the architectural limitations discussed in Section 4, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed numerical implementation, sampling details, and Python code-access footnote are unchanged. No additional reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Marchetti et al. (2025) receives bibliographic reformatting; the Trager et al. (2019) reference merely moves across a page break.

P1.justification: Changes include a grammatical correction in Section 3.3, localized rewriting and paragraph merging in Appendix A.6, equivalent L notation around Equation 28, and version-stamp and bibliography edits. Section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Local reflow alters theorem and proof spacing, shifts Figure 4 vertically, and moves a reference from page 11 to page 10. All four figures retain their content, captions, and numbering.

improvement.justification: Adding L≠0 excludes a zero-output counterexample permitted by v2, improving the precision of Theorem 3.7. Appendix A.6 makes its factorization argument more explicit, although rank(M_i)>1 alone still does not establish the asserted irreducibility, so the proof is not fully repaired. With the main conclusions and empirical evidence unchanged, the overall gain is limited.
